title: Panaji | Government of Goa
text: Panaji, also called Panjim, is the capital of the Indian state of Goa and the headquarters of North Goa district.

title: Brief History of Goa | Government of Goa
text: Goa is administratively divided into two districts: North Goa, headquartered at Panaji, and South Goa, headquartered at Margao.

title: Brief History of Goa | Government of Goa
text: The official language of Goa is Konkani written in the Devanagari script. English, Hindi and Marathi are also allowed for official use.

text: Goa was liberated from Portuguese rule on 19 December 1961 through Operation Vijay and became part of the Indian Union.

title: Churches and Convents of Goa | UNESCO
text: The Churches and Convents of Goa in Old Goa are a UNESCO World Heritage property. The Church of Bom Jesus contains the tomb of St Francis Xavier, and the monuments influenced Manueline, Mannerist and Baroque art across Asia.

text: Our solar system contains the Sun, eight planets, five officially named dwarf planets, hundreds of moons, and thousands of asteroids and comets. The eight planets orbit the Sun.

title: Condensation and the Water Cycle | USGS
text: In the water cycle, evaporation changes liquid water into water vapour, condensation changes water vapour into liquid droplets and forms clouds, and precipitation returns water to Earth's surface as rain, snow, sleet or hail.

title: About Goa | Department of Information and Publicity
text: Goa lies on India's Konkan coast, with the Arabian Sea to the west and the Western Ghats to the east. It covers 3,702 square kilometres and has a coastline of about 105 kilometres.

title: Milestones of Goa | Department of Information and Publicity
text: Goa Revolution Day is observed on 18 June. It commemorates Dr Ram Manohar Lohia's 18 June 1946 public action at Margao that helped energise Goa's civil-liberties and freedom movement.

text: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest planet in our solar system. Saturn is the second-largest planet.

title: Our Sun: Facts | NASA Science
text: The Sun is the star at the centre of our solar system. The planets, asteroids and comets orbit it, and its energy supports life on Earth.
